claims.statement: The repository requires Node.js >=22.0.0 and <25.0.0 with npm >=9.0.0, enforced via the root package.json engines field; the Docker image is built on node:22-bookworm-slim.

npm install at the repository root installs all npm workspaces (packages/*) in a single pass; better-sqlite3 compiles a native addon during install, requiring python3/make/g++ when no prebuilt binary is available (the Dockerfile installs this toolchain and later purges it).

npm run dev uses npm-run-all --parallel to start dev:server (tsx watch src/index.ts in @djimitflo/server) and dev:dashboard (vite) concurrently; the Vite dev server runs on port 5173 and proxies /api and /ws to the backend at localhost:3001.

The root build script is an explicit chained workspace order: shared, telegram, agent-catalog, mcp-server, ransomware-module, server, dashboard. Downstream packages consume workspace dependencies through their built dist outputs (e.g. @djimitflo/shared exports dist/index.js and dist/index.d.ts), so the order matters; the dashboard's Vite config is the exception, aliasing @djimitflo/shared directly to shared/src.

The server package runs tsx watch src/index.ts in dev and node dist/index.js (compiled by tsc) via start; in production the server serves the built dashboard from DASHBOARD_PATH instead of the Vite dev server.

The root npm run test pipeline runs four script selftests BEFORE any workspace test: deploy-vps.selftest.sh, wiki-delta-emitter.selftest.sh, live-identity-evidence.test.mjs, and integration-probes.test.mjs; it then builds shared and agent-catalog and only afterwards runs npm run test --workspaces --if-present.

test:changed first builds shared and agent-catalog, then runs vitest --changed across the server, shared, agent-catalog, and mcp-server workspaces; the root vitest.config.mts selects the jsdom environment with no setup files, and the dashboard configures jsdom with globals.

The root type-check script first builds shared, agent-catalog, mcp-server, and ransomware-module (whose dist declarations are type-resolution targets for downstream workspaces) and then runs type-check across all workspaces with --if-present; lint runs eslint per workspace with --if-present.

db:migrate and db:seed run via tsx (no build of server required). migrate runs only when migrate.ts is the process entry point (a require.main===module guard plus an argv[1] filename check, so a bundled operator script never migrates the DB as an import side effect), then executes runMigrations against resolveDbPath(), which resolves DB_PATH, else DJIMITFLO_DB, else <repo>/.data/djimitflo.sqlite; seed populates mock agents via initializeDatabase(). Normal server startup applies the same schema through initializeDatabase(), so these scripts exist to provision a database without booting the API.

Server development config comes from packages/server/.env.example: dev uses a default JWT secret with a warning while config/env.ts validateEnv() process.exit(1)s in production without JWT_SECRET; AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL/PASSWORD create a bootstrap admin only when no users exist; DJIMITFLO_RUNTIME_PROFILE (resolved by config/runtime-profile.ts: api default, operator, autonomous) gates operator integrations and maintenance loops (operator) plus the loop daemon and autonomous/self-modification services (autonomous).

The Dockerfile is a two-stage build: a builder stage installs all dependencies (with the python3/make/g++ native toolchain) and runs the same npm run build workspace chain, and a runner stage upgrades the base image, installs ca-certificates git python3-minimal curl procps libatomic1 via apt, pins the gh CLI as a static .deb via ARG GH_CLI_VERSION=2.100.0 (verified with gh --version), installs the pinned Atomic Agent release tarball (version + per-arch sha256 verified, symlinked to /usr/local/bin/atomic-agent, probed with atomic-agent --version), pins the global agent runtime CLIs @openai/codex@0.146.0, opencode-ai@1.18.10 and @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.282 with immediate git/codex/opencode/claude --version probes, creates the non-root djimitflo user/group at uid/gid 1001 and chowns /data to it, installs production dependencies only with better-sqlite3 smoke-tested via an in-memory open before the build toolchain is purged, bakes build provenance env vars (DJIMITFLO_COMMIT_SHA, DJIMITFLO_BUILD_COMMIT/TIME/SOURCE) from the VCS_REF/BUILD_TIME/BUILD_SOURCE build args, and runs as the non-root djimitflo user with VOLUME /data, ENTRYPOINT docker-entrypoint.sh and CMD node packages/server/dist/index.js.

docker-entrypoint.sh creates /data and BACKUP_DIR (default /data/backups) if missing, prints startup info, hard-fails with exit 1 when NODE_ENV=production and JWT_SECRET is unset, and finally execs the container CMD so the node process replaces the shell.

docker-compose.yml declares a single djimitflo service that builds from the Dockerfile, publishes ${DJIMITFLO_HOST_PORT:-3001}:3001, loads env from .env.docker, mounts the named volume djimitflo-data at /data, restarts unless stopped, and healthchecks http://localhost:3001/health every 30s; /data holds the SQLite database (/data/djimitflo.sqlite) and backups (/data/backups), making the volume the persistence contract across container replacement.

The root npm run test pipeline is a chained script that runs script-level selftests before any workspace test: bash scripts/deploy-vps.selftest.sh (fixture-compose checks of the VPS deployer scripts/deploy-vps.sh, including image/commit/mount rewrite and rollback), bash scripts/wiki-delta-emitter.selftest.sh, node scripts/live-identity-evidence.test.mjs and node scripts/integration-probes.test.mjs; it then builds @djimitflo/shared and @djimitflo/agent-catalog (their dist outputs are what test imports resolve under tsx type-stripping) and only afterwards runs npm run test --workspaces --if-present.

The repository defines two Stryker mutation lanes: test:mutation runs stryker run against stryker.config.js (curated critical code spans in approval-service, tool-broker, docker-sandbox-executor and runtime-governance, StringLiteral/ObjectLiteral excluded, vitest runner with vitest.mutation.config.ts limited to six named server test files, score thresholds high 85 / low 75 / break 70), and test:mutation:grounded runs node scripts/mutation-gain.mjs.

scripts/mutation-gain.mjs (test:mutation:grounded) requires MUTATE_FILE (source to mutate) and MUTATE_TEST (test under evaluation); it runs Stryker twice via stryker.service.config.mjs — once against the committed HEAD version of the test written to a temporary .mutation-baseline.test.ts, once against the working-tree test — and exits 0 only when the after score gains at least MUTATE_MIN_GAIN points (default 10) or reaches 90; with neither env var set it skips with exit 0 so hosts can list it unconditionally in loop-daemon check scripts.

stryker.service.config.mjs mutates exactly the MUTATE_FILE path, reports JSON to MUTATE_REPORT (default a tmpdir file), and points the vitest runner at vitest.service-mutation.config.ts, a node-environment config whose include is solely [process.env.MUTATE_TEST ?? 'none'] with a 30s timeout, so only the single test file under scrutiny runs against the mutants.

The gh CLI is installed in the runner image because the server's PR-review service shells out to it for PR comments and Check Runs, and the global agent runtimes are pinned to keep the production worker surface equal to the runtimes accepted by /swarms/runtime-readiness; the Dockerfile comments state both rationales.
